objective.value: Achieve complete de novo biosynthesis of carminic acid (6) from glucose in engineered Escherichia coli by (i) optimizing a type II PKS machinery from Photorhabdus luminescens with cyclases ZhuI/ZhuJ for flavokermesic acid (3) production, (ii) identifying unknown hydroxylase and C-glucosyltransferase for later steps via biochemical reaction analysis, (iii) enhancing these enzymes by homology modeling/docking-guided mutagenesis, and (iv) fed-batch fermentation of the final strain.
objective.notes: Secondary demonstrated objective: production of aloesin (8) using the engineered GtCGT mutant (results_and_discussion_p038-p041).

hypothesis.value: A complete carminic acid pathway can be constructed in E. coli by combining a soluble type II minimal PKS with heterologous cyclases, and the two missing reactions (hydroxylation of 3 to 4; C-glucosylation of 3 to 5) can be filled by enzyme candidates selected via biochemical reaction analysis and improved by docking-simulation-guided mutagenesis.

inference.rationale: The paper does not state a formal hypothesis; it is reconstructed from the stated strategy in access_p006 and introduction_p010 and from the bottleneck observation in results_and_discussion_p022 (WT DnrF/GtCGT activities insufficient).

hypothesis.notes: Implicit hypothesis; never stated as a single hypothesis sentence.

experiments.purpose: Obtain a soluble, functional type II minimal PKS platform in E. coli for octaketide shunt products 1 and 2
experiments.intervention: Combinatorial expression of P. luminescens type II PKS components; selection of antDEF + antB (PPTase) + antG (CoA ligase) construct
experiments.readout: titers of 1 and 2 by LC-MS/MS; NMR confirmation
experiments.analysis: two-tailed Student's t-test with Bonferroni correction
experiments.outcome: antDEFBG gave highest 1 and 2 titers (P = 2.1e-3 and 8.2e-4); chosen for further studies

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: heterologous construct assembly by authors; Q2: performed in this paper; Q3: selected platform used in all downstream work.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Selection/assembly of the core pathway enzyme machinery (minimal PKS + auxiliary enzymes).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Known type II minimal PKS solubility failure in non-Streptomyces hosts; P. luminescens AntDEF reported soluble and functional in E. coli (MiBiG-based identification, ref 31).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers of 1 and 2 with statistics.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Best construct chosen by screening component combinations; no mechanistic claim for why this combination is optimal beyond highest titer.
alternatives_considered: other type II PKS component combinations (Supplementary Note S1)

experiments.purpose: Choose between type II and type III PKS machinery for flavokermesic acid (3) production
experiments.intervention: Parallel expression of AntDEFBG+ZhuIJ (two plasmids) vs AaPKS5+ZhuIJ (pET-AaPKS5)
experiments.control: type III PKS construct as comparator
experiments.outcome: type II system: 15.1 mg/L vs type III 4.3 mg/L (P = 4.1e-4); type II pursued

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: two pathway constructs built and compared; Q2: this paper; Q3: determined the platform for all later steps.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Platform/pathway route selection.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Type II and type III machineries gave similar 1/2 titers (P = 0.28, 0.85), so both were tested for cyclized product 3.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured 3 titers with significance.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Empirical head-to-head comparison; choice based on measured titer, not an a priori mechanism.

experiments.purpose: Reduce two-plasmid metabolic burden for 3 production
experiments.intervention: Cloning zhuIJ into pDS00-antDEFBG to create single plasmid pFK
experiments.outcome: 88.0 mg/L of 3 (P = 1.8e-5), large enhancement over two-plasmid 15.1 mg/L

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: new construct built; Q2: this paper; Q3: pFK became the standard backbone (FK strain).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Expression configuration/burden balancing of pathway genes.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Metabolic burden of maintaining two plasmids; need for higher 3 titers.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer increase with strong significance.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Stated rationale: reduce metabolic burden; authors additionally hypothesize colocalization increases transient minimal PKS-cyclase complex formation (hedged: 'is thought to have').
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When interacting pathway enzymes (type II minimal PKS and its cyclases) are expressed from two plasmids in E. coli and burden limits product formation, apply consolidation onto a single plasmid, because reduced plasmid burden and colocalized expression can increase effective enzyme interplay, as demonstrated for flavokermesic acid production.

experiments.purpose: Prevent oxidative polymerization loss of 3
experiments.intervention: Ascorbic acid supplementation to the medium
experiments.conditions: flask culture; culture turning bright red to brownish
experiments.outcome: titer of 3 increased to 154.9 mg/L (P = 4.2e-3)

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: medium/condition change; Q2: this paper; Q3: retained in subsequent 3 production.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Management of product loss via side reaction (oxidative polymerization).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Culture gradually turned from bright red to brownish, suggesting polymerization of 3 into melanin-like compounds.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer increase.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Oxidation-driven polymerization mechanism invoked (hedged 'it was thought that'), with literature analogy to similar aromatic polyketides (ref 39).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When an aromatic polyketide product (flavokermesic acid) undergoes oxidative polymerization during E. coli culture, apply antioxidant supplementation (ascorbic acid), because preventing excess oxidation preserves the soluble product and increases the measured titer.

experiments.purpose: Increase malonyl-CoA supply for 3 production
experiments.intervention: Overexpression of C. glutamicum accBCD1 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase)
experiments.control: pFK + ascorbic acid without accBCD1 OE
experiments.outcome: 180.3 mg/L of 3 (P = 0.105, NS under Bonferroni); carried forward nonetheless

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: overexpression; Q2: applied to this pathway in this paper; Q3: accBCD1 OE reused in final carminic acid strain.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor (malonyl-CoA) supply enhancement.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: 3 is an octaketide built from malonyl-CoA; increasing the malonyl-CoA pool was pursued to raise titers.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer, though the increase was not statistically significant here (P = 0.105).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit precursor-pool mechanism; strategy additionally anchored in the group's prior report (ref 5).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When producing malonyl-CoA-derived aromatic polyketides in E. coli, apply overexpression of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (accBCD1), because enlarging the malonyl-CoA pool supports higher polyketide chain synthesis, as shown for flavokermesic acid and carminic acid.

experiments.purpose: Increase malonyl-CoA availability via knockdown
experiments.intervention: pabA knockdown (anti-pabA synthetic sRNA)
experiments.outcome: tested as alternative malonyl-CoA strategy (Figure 1d); accBCD1 OE route emphasized downstream

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: sRNA knockdown applied; Q2: applied here (strategy from prior paper); Q3: pabA KD reused in carminic acid and aloesin strains.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor supply via knockdown of a consuming/competing gene.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Need to enlarge malonyl-CoA pool (same as EXP-05).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured in Figure 1d; exact per-group values only from figure.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicitly adopted from the group's recent report (ref 5, biosensor-identified pabA knockdown); no new mechanistic derivation here.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When increasing the malonyl-CoA pool in E. coli polyketide production, apply pabA knockdown, because prior biosensor-based screening identified pabA silencing as malonyl-CoA-elevating, as transferred here from the group's earlier system.

experiments.analysis: t-test with Bonferroni; CFM-ID annotation; in vitro enzyme assay confirmation
experiments.outcome: DnrF gave highest 4 titer (P = 6.6e-7); isomer 4' also observed; conversion confirmed in vitro

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: heterologous expression of candidates; Q2: this paper; Q3: DnrF became the pathway hydroxylase.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Elucidation/completion of a missing pathway step.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Only trace 4 formed (possibly by inherent E. coli oxygenases); no monooxygenase for this reaction had been reported.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers plus in vitro confirmation.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Candidates shortlisted by literature/database biochemical reaction analysis, then experimentally screened; winner chosen by measured activity.

experiments.purpose: Functionally express the native DcUGT2 C-glucosyltransferase in E. coli
experiments.intervention: Expression of DcUGT2 variants: full-length, Ntr-DcUGT2, Ctr-DcUGT2, Ntr-Ctr-DcUGT2, and OmpA signal peptide fusions

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: rational construct engineering; Q2: this paper; Q3: failure redirected the search toward the CGT candidate screen (EXP-09).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Engineering of the enzyme's localization/solubility features (signal peptide, transmembrane helix).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: DcUGT2 is glycosylated, membrane-bound (C-terminal TM helix, eukaryotic N-terminal signal peptide), expected not to work in E. coli.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured negative result across all constructs.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Deletions/fusions target specific sequence features (signal peptide, TM helix) with a stated membrane-targeting rationale (ref 48).
alternatives_considered: direct screening of alternative CGTs (taken up in EXP-09)

experiments.purpose: Identify a C-glucosyltransferase converting 3 to dcII (5)
experiments.intervention: Separate introduction of 8 CGT candidates (IroB, ZmCGT, FeCGT, MiCGT, OsCGT, GmCGT, GtCGT, AvCGT)

experiments.analysis: t-test; CFM-ID-based isomer assignment; NMR of 5; in vitro assay confirmation
experiments.outcome: Only GtCGT converted 3 to 5 (major) with O-glucoside isomer 5'; ZmCGT gave 5''

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: heterologous expression screen; Q2: this paper; Q3: GtCGT became the pathway CGT.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Missing-step enzyme identification.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Native DcUGT2 nonfunctional in E. coli (EXP-08); C-glucosylation rarely reported in bacteria.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured conversion and structural confirmation.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Candidate set prioritized from reported E. coli-active UDP-glycosyltransferases; selection by experimental outcome.
alternatives_considered: IroB (chosen partly because it is E. coli-native)

experiments.purpose: Boost UDP-glucose supply for C-glucosylation
experiments.intervention: Overexpression of galU, pgm and ndk
experiments.control: FK + GtCGT without the three-gene overexpression
experiments.outcome: 5 production increased 2.3-fold

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: overexpression; Q2: this paper; Q3: cofactor-supply module carried into carminic acid work.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Cofactor/co-substrate (UDP-glucose) supply enhancement.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: C-glucosylation requires a high UDP-glucose pool.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured 2.3-fold increase.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit donor-pool mechanism; specific gene set follows Leonard et al. (ref 60).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When C-glucosylation of an aromatic polyketide in E. coli is limited by UDP-glucose availability, apply galU-pgm-ndk overexpression, because these enzymes enhance UDP-glucose generation and UDP recycling.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integration of all validated pathway steps.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: All individual conversion steps had been verified, so complete reconstitution was attempted.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured negative result.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Pathway reconstitution logic from individually verified steps; bottleneck attribution to downstream enzyme activity is stated (as speculation).

experiments.purpose: Enhance DnrF activity toward 3
experiments.intervention: Testing of 29 DnrF mutants (top 20 docking-score mutants + 9 structure-rational picks; MODELLER homology model on PDB 3IHG, PyRosetta docking)

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: point mutagenesis; Q2: this paper; Q3: P217K used in final strain.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting enzyme improvement via structure-guided mutagenesis.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: WT DnrF activity insufficient to convert accumulated 3 (EXP-11).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Mutant selection was driven by predictive docking scores (requires experimental confirmation); experimental titers and kinetics later provided hard validation.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Mutants chosen from a computational screen by docking score; authors themselves state the improvement was 'due to an unknown reason such as higher specific activity' - mechanistic explanations offered are hedged post-hoc interpretations.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Combination of beneficial enzyme mutations.

ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer decrease.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: No explicit mechanistic reason given for expecting synergy; simple additivity assumption, falsified experimentally.

experiments.purpose: Enhance GtCGT activity toward 3
experiments.intervention: Testing of 34 GtCGT mutants (top 20 docking-score + 14 rational picks; homology model on PDB 6JTD)

experiments.outcome: 6 mutants improved 5; V93Q best (2.8-fold), Y193F second (>2-fold)

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: point mutagenesis; Q2: this paper; Q3: fed into double-mutant design (EXP-15).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting enzyme improvement.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: WT GtCGT activity insufficient for complete conversion of 3 (EXP-11).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Selection driven by predictive docking scores; experimental titers gave later hard validation.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Docking-score-based screening of in silico mutant library.

experiments.purpose: Combine beneficial GtCGT mutations
experiments.intervention: Construction of GtCGT V93Q/Y193F double mutant
experiments.analysis: structure-based H-bond analysis; AutoDock Vina with transition-state analogue; kinetics
experiments.outcome: 5.3-fold higher 5 titer; Vmax +18.2% (P=0.048), KM 6.30->5.07 uM (NS), Vmax/KM +46.8%; expression unchanged; chosen for CA and ALS strains

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: new mutant built; Q2: this paper; Q3: became the final CGT for both products.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Structure-guided combination of active-site mutations.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Single mutants V93Q and Y193F each improved 5; model predicted Y193F frees Gln93 to H-bond the C6 hydroxyl of 3, orienting it for C2 C-glucosylation.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Combination rationale rests on homology-model/docking predictions (predictive); subsequent kinetics gave hard confirmation of improved catalytic efficiency.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives an explicit structural mechanism (H-bond network and ligand orientation at C2) for combining the two mutations.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When engineering a C-glucosyltransferase for higher activity toward an aromatic polyketide substrate in E. coli, apply structure-guided active-site mutations that improve ligand orientation for C-glucosylation, because proper hydrogen-bond-mediated positioning of the aglycone favors C-C bond formation at the target carbon, as shown for GtCGT V93Q/Y193F on flavokermesic acid.

experiments.purpose: Increase aloesone (7) supply before C-glucosylation to aloesin (8)
experiments.host: E. coli BL21(DE3) harboring pWAS-anti-pabA and pBBR1-zwf
experiments.intervention: Additional RpALS copy on compatible plasmid (pCDF-RpALS + pRSF-RpALS)
experiments.control: single pCDF-RpALS strain (prior 30.9 mg/L from ref 5)
experiments.outcome: 102.1 mg/L of 7

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: gene copy-number increase; Q2: this paper (prior strain from ref 5 extended here); Q3: enabled aloesin production attempts.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Expression-level balancing of the pathway synthase.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Higher 7 titers needed before testing C-glucosylation to 8; prior strain made only 30.9 mg/L.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Stated rationale: further increasing RpALS expression level to enhance production (gene dosage-flux relationship).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When aloesone production from glucose in E. coli is limited by aloesone synthase level, apply additional expression of RpALS from a compatible plasmid, because raising synthase dosage increases flux toward the heptaketide product.

experiments.purpose: Produce aloesin (8) by repurposing the engineered CGT
experiments.intervention: Introduction of pCDF-GtCGT or pCDF-GtCGTmut; then ALS strain with pCDF-RpALS-GtCGTmut
experiments.readout: titer of 8 by LC-MS/MS vs authentic standard
experiments.outcome: GtCGTmut strain produced 8 at 0.060 ug/L (P = 0.046 vs WT CGT); ALS strain 0.30 ug/L (P = 0.011); first report of microbial 8 production

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: new pathway assembled; Q2: this paper; Q3: demonstrated general applicability of the engineered CGT.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Completion of an unknown pathway step with a promiscuous engineered enzyme.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: The CGT converting 7 to 8 had not been identified; GtCGT V93Q/Y193F was available and active on a structurally similar polyketide (3).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured product confirmed against authentic standard.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit substrate-similarity hypothesis: test whether the CGT applies to 'other similar C-glucosylation reactions'.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When the native CGT for C-glucosylating an aromatic polyketide aglycone is unknown, apply an engineered CGT validated on a structurally similar polyketide, because substrate promiscuity can extend to related aglycones, as shown for aloesin production by GtCGT V93Q/Y193F in E. coli.

experiments.purpose: Produce carminic acid (6) from glucose with enhanced downstream enzymes
experiments.intervention: Construction of CA strain (BAP1 harboring pFK and pCA carrying dnrF and GtCGT mutant genes; exact plasmid definition requires_supplement)
experiments.readout: titer of 6 by LC-MS/MS (MRM) vs commercial standard
experiments.outcome: 22.2 ug/L of 6 from glucose; first bacterial production of 6

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: strain integration with mutant enzymes; Q2: this paper; Q3: base strain for all further carminic acid optimization.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integration of engineered enzymes into the full pathway.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: WT DnrF/GtCGT gave no detectable 6 despite 180.3 mg/L of 3; downstream activities speculated insufficient.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer of 6.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Bottleneck logic: replacing activity-limiting downstream enzymes with validated higher-activity mutants.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When an accumulated pathway intermediate (flavokermesic acid) is not converted to the final product because downstream enzyme activities are insufficient, apply replacement of those enzymes with activity-enhanced variants, because downstream catalytic capacity limits end-product formation in the carminic acid pathway in E. coli.

experiments.purpose: Further enhance 6 production via precursor/cofactor supply modules
experiments.intervention: accBCD1 overexpression, pabA knockdown, and/or galU-pgm-ndk overexpression, alone and in combinations
experiments.outcome: CA-ACC (accBCD1 OE): 74.9 ug/L, 3.4-fold (P = 2.3e-3); other module outcomes shown in Figure 5a (exact values requires figure/supplement reading)

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: overexpression/knockdown modules; Q2: this paper; Q3: CA-ACC selected as final strain.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor (malonyl-CoA) and co-substrate (UDP-glucose) supply enhancement.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: CA strain titer (22.2 ug/L) far below the 180.3 mg/L intermediate capacity; supply modules previously beneficial for 3 and 5.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers with significance for CA-ACC.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Same precursor-supply mechanisms as EXP-05/EXP-06/EXP-10, transferred from earlier pathway stages.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When carminic acid production in E. coli is limited after pathway completion, apply accBCD1 overexpression to enlarge the malonyl-CoA pool, because precursor supply limits flux through the type II PKS backbone, as shown by the 3.4-fold gain in CA-ACC.

experiments.purpose: Improve folding of heterologous enzymes for 6 production
experiments.intervention: Coexpression of chaperones DnaK-DnaJ-GrpE, GroES/EL, trigger factor, or ClpB
experiments.outcome: dnaKJ-grpE: 48.9 ug/L (P = 2.4e-4); groES/EL: 31.3 ug/L (P = 0.024, NS after correction); TF and ClpB without significant gains

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: chaperone overexpression; Q2: this paper; Q3: dnaKJ-grpE advanced to combination testing.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Improving functional expression/folding of pathway enzymes.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Multiple heterologous enzymes (type II PKS components historically inclusion-body-prone) may fold poorly in E. coli.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Chaperone sets employed per established recombinant-protein folding practice (ref 69) with a folding-facilitation mechanism.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When heterologous polyketide pathway enzymes are poorly folded in E. coli, apply coexpression of chaperones such as DnaKJ-GrpE or GroES/EL, because chaperone-assisted folding increases the functional enzyme pool, as shown for carminic acid production.

experiments.purpose: Test combination of accBCD1 OE and dnaKJ-grpE OE; choose final strain
experiments.intervention: Simultaneous overexpression of accBCD1 and dnaKJ-grpE
experiments.outcome: 44.4 ug/L; no further increase over CA-ACC (74.9 ug/L); CA-ACC selected as final strain

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: module combination; Q2: this paper; Q3: negative result fixed the final strain choice (CA-ACC).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integration/screening of beneficial module combinations.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: accBCD1 OE and dnaKJ-grpE OE each improved 6 titers individually; authors reasoned the combination might increase further.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer showing no additive gain.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Stated reasoning that simultaneous supply and folding improvements would further increase titer; falsified experimentally.

experiments.purpose: Assess production performance of final strain CA-ACC at bioreactor scale
experiments.intervention: pH-stat fed-batch fermentation in 6.6 L bioreactor with IPTG induction (two independent runs)
experiments.readout: time profiles of DCW, 6, intermediates 3-5, shunt products 1-2
experiments.outcome: 0.65 and 0.61 mg/L of 6 (good reproducibility; abstract mean 0.63+/-0.02 mg/L); 3 accumulated to 3.66 g/L, indicating incomplete downstream conversion

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q3 fails: fed-batch assessed the already-selected final strain's performance without introducing a new design action within this paper; the 3-accumulation observation informs only future work.

experiments.purpose: Compare flavonoid C-glucosylation efficiency of GtCGT vs GtCGT V93Q/Y193F
experiments.host: E. coli BL21(DE3) harboring pCDF-GtCGT or pCDF-GtCGTmut
experiments.intervention: none (feeding assay on existing constructs)
experiments.conditions: flask culture with exogenous feeding of luteolin, apigenin, naringenin
experiments.readout: in vivo conversion efficiency to flavonoid C-glucosides
experiments.outcome: GtCGT V93Q/Y193F showed generally decreased conversion of its native-type flavonoid substrates, indicating an activity trade-off from engineering toward polyketides

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: substrate-scope measurement of existing constructs; no new engineering action.
